notes.evidenceGrammar: PATH_LINE_RE stays two hand-typed regexes, one per validator, because \w and \d are Unicode-wide in Python and ASCII-only in JavaScript; a shared source would compile the same pattern into two different meanings. ADR-0185.

refusals.criteriaHeadingWithoutItems: '## Acceptance criteria' heading has no '- [ ]' items; plain '- ' bullets don't count
refusals.claimIsGlob: '## Files claimed' names `{entry}`, which is a glob rather than a path. A claim is one file: it is what one implementer edits, and it is what the reconciler holds against every live run, so a pattern standing for a whole lane keeps this ticket from starting while anything in that lane runs, and keeps anything in that lane from starting while this one does. Name each file the work edits, one per line.
refusals.claimTooWide: '## Files claimed' names {count} files; {limit} is the ceiling. Lane 04's author inlines every claimed file into one prompt, so a claim this wide spends the whole lane budget on its first pass and dies at author-repair with nothing authored (#539). Split it into slices of one subject each.
refusals.checkReadsTracker: acceptance criterion checks the tracker instead of the tree: `{command}` reads GitHub or the network, so it answers the same whether or not this ticket's diff exists. Check what the work changes in the checkout; a fact about production belongs to a spec's one criterion
